title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is designed to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems. It sets standards for energy use, resource consumption, and lifecycle emissions, requiring transparency and accountability from AI developers and operators.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that mandates that medical decisions and patient care must be performed or supervised by licensed human doctors rather than by artificial intelligence systems alone. It requires that AI tools can only assist doctors, not replace them, ensuring that patients receive direct human oversight and accountability in their medical treatment.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act is a proposed law that seeks to boost the global competitiveness of domestic AI companies by encouraging the export of the complete AI ecosystem—from hardware and software to data and models. It aims to provide incentives, streamline regulatory processes, and support innovation to help U.S. businesses lead in AI technology worldwide.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a legislative proposal that aims to promote the development and widespread adoption of open‑source artificial intelligence technologies. By encouraging collaboration, transparency, and shared governance, it seeks to foster innovation while ensuring that AI models are built and used responsibly and benefit society at large.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: This Act sets rules for how AI systems can be used to serve veterans, emphasizing transparency, safety, and fairness. It requires oversight and safeguards to protect veterans from bias or misuse of AI technologies.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a federal law that aims to create national standards and best‑practice guidelines for protecting AI systems from cyber attacks and other security threats. It calls for close collaboration among government agencies, industry partners, and academic researchers to develop secure AI technologies, conduct regular risk assessments, and establish rapid response procedures for any AI‑related security incidents.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: This act aims to reduce bias in automated decision‑making systems by setting clear standards and oversight for algorithm design and deployment. It requires transparency, testing, and accountability measures to ensure fair and equitable outcomes for all users.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to protect AI models from being illegally copied, shared, or sold. It defines the theft of AI models as a crime, sets out penalties for infringers, and creates a framework for reporting and prosecuting such violations.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that deploy automated decision‑making tools to assess and document the social and economic impact of their algorithms, including bias and fairness risks. It also creates a federal oversight body that will audit these assessments and enforce compliance to protect consumers from unfair or discriminatory algorithmic practices.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes mandatory standards for the safety, reliability, and performance of AI systems used in defense, requiring rigorous testing and documentation before deployment. It also creates a reporting framework that obligates military organizations to report incidents, errors, and performance data to oversight bodies, ensuring continuous improvement and accountability.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that aims to create a framework for responsible AI development and use. It focuses on ensuring transparency, accountability, and safety while encouraging innovation and protecting consumer rights.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires Chinese companies and research labs to submit regular reports on the computing power, energy usage, and performance of their AI systems. This law is meant to increase transparency, help regulators monitor environmental impact, and promote responsible AI development.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This act is designed to protect the integrity of elections by limiting the use of deceptive AI that could manipulate voters or spread misinformation. It requires greater transparency, accountability, and restrictions on AI tools that might interfere with democratic processes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a proposed law that would require companies developing AI systems capable of self‑modification to regularly report their internal changes and performance to a designated oversight agency. It also sets up clear safety and accountability standards, ensuring that such AI can be tested, audited, and monitored before and during deployment to protect against unintended or harmful behavior.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new AI data centers to address environmental, energy, and regulatory concerns. It requires a review period to assess impacts and develop guidelines for responsible future data center development.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is a proposed law that seeks to shield households from the high electricity expenses generated by AI data centers. It aims to do this by regulating energy usage, offering subsidies or tax credits, and encouraging more efficient technology to keep costs affordable for families.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on constructing new AI data centers. It aims to address environmental and infrastructure concerns while policymakers assess best practices for future AI infrastructure.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed legislation that seeks to establish clear rules and safeguards for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence. It focuses on protecting privacy, reducing bias, and ensuring transparency, while fostering responsible innovation and collaboration between industry and regulators.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive safety standards for AI‑powered toys that children play with, covering design, data handling, and user interaction. It aims to protect children from risks such as privacy breaches, inappropriate content, and unsafe behavior by mandating strict compliance and oversight for toy manufacturers and developers.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to safeguard the personal information of children and teenagers from misuse by artificial intelligence systems. It sets strict data handling and consent rules for companies that collect or process AI-related data involving young users.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI developers and operators to submit detailed reports on their AI systems' capabilities, usage, and impact. It aims to increase transparency, monitor AI development, and ensure that AI technologies are used responsibly within China.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a regulatory framework designed to govern the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence models, focusing on safety, reliability, and public trust. It mandates transparency requirements, risk assessment protocols, and accountability measures to ensure AI systems are ethical, secure, and aligned with societal values.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill proposes a system for creating and sharing detailed “functional bills of materials” for artificial intelligence products, aiming to improve transparency and traceability of AI components and capabilities. It also includes additional provisions related to regulatory oversight, safety, and other purposes that support responsible AI deployment.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act proposes establishing a national workforce strategy to ensure that employees across industries have the skills and knowledge to responsibly develop and use AI systems. The act would create training programs, certifications, and research grants to build public confidence and promote ethical AI deployment.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent artificial intelligence companies from raising prices unfairly and manipulating wages in the industry. It introduces regulations to ensure fair pricing practices and protect workers from AI-driven wage suppression.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes rules for the use of artificial intelligence in agriculture, aiming to protect farmers, consumers, and the environment. It sets standards for data privacy, safety, and ethical deployment of AI tools in farming practices.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This act aims to encourage the development and deployment of AI technologies in the financial sector by providing a supportive regulatory framework. It establishes guidelines for responsible use, safeguards, and collaboration between regulators and industry to promote innovation while protecting consumers.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act seeks to encourage banks, lenders and investment firms to adopt AI tools by easing regulatory constraints and setting clear safety guidelines. It also introduces rules for data sharing, ethical use, and consumer protection to ensure the new technologies benefit customers without compromising security or fairness.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a U.S. law designed to boost the nation’s AI workforce by supporting education, training, and research programs that develop AI expertise. It also encourages partnerships between industry, academia, and government to create jobs, accelerate innovation, and ensure the U.S. stays competitive in the global AI race.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the development and operation of AI data centers on any federally owned or managed land. This measure is intended to protect federal property, curb large-scale energy use, and reduce potential security or environmental risks associated with AI infrastructure.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is designed to weave artificial‑intelligence education into the K‑12 curriculum by establishing clear standards and providing schools with the resources they need. It will fund teacher training, student learning programs, and equitable access to AI tools so that both educators and students are ready to navigate an AI‑driven world.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to weave AI education into primary and secondary school curricula, giving students the foundational knowledge and skills they need to understand and responsibly use AI technologies. The act also sets standards, provides teacher training, and allocates resources to help schools build AI readiness and ensure students are prepared for a future where AI is ubiquitous.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 proposes a comprehensive regulatory framework for artificial intelligence in the United States, aiming to ensure that AI systems are safe, transparent, and trustworthy while fostering innovation and competitiveness. The act outlines risk‑based requirements for AI development and deployment, mandates certification and oversight for high‑risk applications, and establishes penalties for non‑compliance to protect consumers and the public.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The “Understanding AI in the Classroom Act” is intended to guide educators on how to responsibly integrate AI tools into teaching and learning, ensuring that students and teachers understand the benefits and risks. It aims to establish clear rules for data privacy, transparency, and ethical use of AI in schools.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says that all Americans and local communities affected by the building or running of an artificial‑intelligence data center must have a right to know what is happening.  It also stresses that those communities should have the power to influence decisions that impact their environment and daily life.
